seo.description: Landing page reference for an agency or studio — Inter, #F3F3F3 base, 0.1s transitions and React and Tailwind CSS. Copy the prompt or open it staged in Studio.

h1: Creative Studio — Agencies & Studios Landing Page Design
tagline: “Creative Studios Built Around Elevating Your Vision Into Striking Reality” — the whole landing page is composed around that line, down to the animation timings.
summary: Landing page reference for an agency or studio — Inter, #F3F3F3 base, 0.1s transitions and React and Tailwind CSS.
about: Creative Studio gives an agency or studio a finished first screen and the numbers that produced it. “Creative Studios Built Around Elevating Your Vision Into Striking Reality” is the line the layout is built to carry. Colour is limited to white #F3F3F3 underneath and indigo #5E0ED7 for the type, set in Inter. The build is React and Tailwind CSS; every measurement in it is written down, which is what makes it reusable. Motion is limited to 0.1s transitions. Use it as the reference when you are building an agency or studio landing page and want a finished composition instead of a starting point.

layout.title: A navigation bar that gets out of the way
layout.body: A slim bar sits over the landing page with the wordmark on the left and the links set in Inter, so the composition reads as content first and chrome second. A mobile overlay takes over below the tablet breakpoint. The bar sits over the 640x462 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: One scale for type and frame
layout.body: The layout is solved against fixed values (10px spacing steps and 0.1s transitions), which is what keeps the first screen composed at any width. The frame proportions are recorded with the sizes, so a rebuild gets the aspect right as well.

layout.title: Navigation without a background
layout.body: The mobile menu is part of the brief, so the collapsed state is designed rather than improvised. Design the collapsed state before adding a sixth link.

layout.title: The sizes are in the brief, not in a scale
layout.body: Spacing is quoted the same way (10px spacing steps and 0.1s transitions), not as a scale that grows on its own.

motion.title: Durations from the brief
motion.body: One duration covers the interactions (0.1s), which is what keeps hover and press reading as one system. Easing is specified alongside the duration (0.1s), so a rebuild cannot quietly substitute a different feel.

motion.title: Almost no motion
motion.body: There is no scroll library here: the 640x462 composition holds still and only the elements that respond to you move. There is no animation library in the brief, which keeps the rebuild small.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.weights: Weight not fixed in the brief
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one face for the whole page

notes: Transitions are specified at 0.1s, which is the value to keep when the palette changes.

Transitions are specified at 0.1s, short enough that the page never feels like it is waiting for an animation.

editorial.title: The argument this landing page makes
editorial.body: Most agency pages add another section when the first screen is weak. This one removes options instead: navigation, the headline, the stats row, the card grid and the feature list, in that order, and nothing that repeats the offer. It gives a agency reader the shortest honest route to the offer.

editorial.title: What to change first in Creative Studio
editorial.body: Suppose you only have one afternoon. Change the headline and the action label, leave 10px spacing steps and 0.1s transitions alone, and you have a page that looks intentional. The composition is the reusable part, and it survives a different brand.

editorial.title: The timing behind the landing page
editorial.body: Copy the pattern rather than the values: keep 0.1s transitions and let your own brand set the durations. Nothing animates for its own sake in this landing page.

faq.question: What does the brief behind Creative Studio actually contain?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 640x462, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.

faq.question: How much of Creative Studio depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Creative Studio was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: What drives the motion in Creative Studio?
faq.answer: The motion is specified at the same level of detail as the layout: state changes settle in the 0.1s range. Port the composition first and the timings second, because they are easier to match once the layout holds.
